# API: Message channels

Message channels connect Digital Humans to IM platforms such as WeCom, Feishu and WeChat; notifications send alerts out. Use these operations to connect and disconnect channels, bind chats to Digital Humans, read the transcripts of bound chats, and test notifications. Create channels and enter their credentials in **Settings › Message Channels**.

Paths are relative to your Halo base URL, and every request carries the access password. Set `$HALO_URL` and `$HALO_TOKEN` as in the [quickstart](/en/developers/quickstart); base URL, authentication and error conventions are in the [HTTP API overview](/en/developers/api/).

## Check whether a Feishu bot is actually reachable, not just connected {#post-api-feishu-bot-reachability}

`POST /api/feishu-bot/reachability` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- A Feishu app awaiting administrator release connects normally and receives nothing, so "connected" alone does not mean the bot works. inboundCount 0 with a long connectedSinceMs is the signature of that case. No credentials in this response.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "instanceId": "<instanceId — from GET /api/im-channels/status>"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{state,connectedSinceMs,lastInboundAgoMs,inboundCount,lastError?}}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/feishu-bot/reachability" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"instanceId":"<instanceId — from GET /api/im-channels/status>"}'
```

## List available IM channel provider types and their config fields {#get-api-im-channels-providers}

`GET /api/im-channels/providers` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Schema only. No endpoint here creates an instance from it — the user creates instances in Settings &gt; Message Channels. Schema only (field definitions and empty defaults) — no configured instance data or secrets.

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{type,displayName,description,direction,configFields:[{key,label,type,placeholder?,required?}],defaultConfig}]}
```

**Example**

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## List every chat thread a digital human has, its own and IM ones {#get-api-im-sessions}

`GET /api/im-sessions` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Optional ?appId= narrows it to one digital human. This is the only listing of its threads — there is no sessions/list beside sessions/create.
- source says what a thread is: "local" = a named thread the user created in Halo, "im" = a real chat with a person on an IM platform, "http" = created through this API.
- Reading or writing one thread needs a conversationId, which is not a field here — build it from four fields of the record: app-chat:&lt;appId&gt;:&lt;channel&gt;:&lt;chatType&gt;:&lt;chatId&gt;.
- Only "local" and "http" threads accept a message from this API. An "im" thread is refused on send — this API must not put words into a real conversation with a person.

**Query parameters**: `appId`

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{appId,channel,source:"local"|"im"|"http",chatType:"direct"|"group",chatId,displayName,customName?,proactive,instanceId,pushLinks?:[{appId,autoSync}]}]}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/im-sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## List the IM chats a digital human pushes to through another digital human's bot {#get-api-im-sessions-linked}

`GET /api/im-sessions/linked` <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Each record is the session as the bot's own digital human holds it (its appId is that one). The asking digital human's entry in pushLinks says whether its run results are auto-pushed there.

**Query parameters**: `appId` (required)

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:[{appId,channel,chatType,chatId,displayName,instanceId,pushLinks:[{appId,autoSync}]}]}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -s "$HALO_URL/api/im-sessions/linked?appId=<appId — a uuid from GET /api/apps>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN"
```

## Remove a chat binding from the IM session registry {#post-api-im-sessions-remove}

`POST /api/im-sessions/remove` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- removed:false means no matching session was found — not an error. Only removes display metadata (custom name, proactive flag, other digital humans' push links to it); the chat re-registers itself on its next inbound message, message history is not stored here.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "appId": "<appId — a uuid from GET /api/apps>",
  "channel": "wecom-bot",
  "chatId": "<chatId — from GET /api/im-sessions>"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true,data:{removed:boolean}}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/im-sessions/remove" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appId":"<appId — a uuid from GET /api/apps>","channel":"wecom-bot","chatId":"<chatId — from GET /api/im-sessions>"}'
```

```json
{
  "appId": "<appId — a uuid from GET /api/apps>",

  -d '{"appId":"<appId — a uuid from GET /api/apps>","channel":"wecom-bot","chatId":"<chatId — from GET /api/im-sessions>","proactive":true}'
```

## Let a digital human push to an IM chat another digital human's bot knows, or stop it {#post-api-im-sessions-set-push-link}

`POST /api/im-sessions/set-push-link` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- link:{autoSync} adds the chat to the digital human's push targets or updates it; autoSync:true also pushes its run results there. link:null removes it.
- Replies in that chat still go to the digital human the bot answers for. 404 when the session does not exist, is not an IM chat, or is the digital human's own.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "appId": "<appId of the digital human that pushes>",
  "session": {
    "appId": "<the session's own appId>",
    "channel": "wecom-bot",
    "chatId": "<chatId — from GET /api/im-sessions>"
  },
  "link": {
    "autoSync": false
  }
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true} or {success:false,error}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/im-sessions/set-push-link" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appId":"<appId of the digital human that pushes>","session":{"appId":"<the session'\''s own appId>","channel":"wecom-bot","chatId":"<chatId — from GET /api/im-sessions>"},"link":{"autoSync":false}}'
```

## Send a test notification through one configured channel {#post-api-notify-channels-test}

`POST /api/notify-channels/test` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- `channelType` is one of `wecom`, `dingtalk`, `feishu`, `email` or `webhook`.
- Delivers a real message: a fixed test text through that channel. The text cannot be changed, so this is a test, not a way to send notifications.
- "No notification channels configured" means none is set up yet; channels are set up in **Settings › Message Channels**.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "channelType": "wecom"
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{"success":true,"data":{...delivery result}}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/notify-channels/test" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channelType":"wecom"}'
```

## Set the bot token for an already-configured WeChat iLink instance {#post-api-weixin-ilink-save-token}

`POST /api/weixin-ilink/save-token` <Badge type="tip" text="Reversible" /> <Badge type="info" text="Assistant" />

- Optional fields: baseUrl, accountId.
- instanceId must already exist (created earlier in the Settings UI) — this route cannot create a new instance, only fill in its token.
- Never echoes the token back in the response.
- {success:false,error:"..."} when instanceId is not found in config.
- Takes over that channel identity immediately — a wrong token silently hijacks it until corrected.

**Request body**

```json
{
  "instanceId": "<instanceId — from GET /api/im-channels/status>",
  "botToken": "..."
}
```

**Response**

```ts
{success:true} or {success:false,error}
```

**Example**

```bash
curl -sX POST "$HALO_URL/api/weixin-ilink/save-token" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HALO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"instanceId":"<instanceId — from GET /api/im-channels/status>","botToken":"..."}'
```
